claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, the stage lock only protects an execution once it is actually running; a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.

In a CodePipeline in SUPERSEDED mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, if enough commits land while the stage is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn, rather than a later execution replacing an earlier waiting one.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
When defining a CodePipeline pipeline, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set to use QUEUED mode, via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline`/`update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link to the AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works.html' documents CodePipeline execution modes.
The page /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists as the docs for the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource, and the resource is described further below in the page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and documents update conflicts.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on the environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a property set on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
The `lockBehavior` stage property in Azure Pipelines defaults to `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in the same way as `lockBehavior: sequential` runs queued stages in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link target /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, with `command: up` and `args: --yes` in this example.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds", located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" has a default value of 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments (prevents concurrent runs).
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` is used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment so that queued runs proceed sequentially.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's execution mode `QUEUED` is a valid pipeline execution mode value.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
